data.summary: All calls share one process, so a single crash, exit or uninterruptible call marks every later input as "timeout" without calling it.

sightings.summary: All calls share one process, so a single crash, exit or uninterruptible call marks every later input as "timeout" without calling it.
sightings.evidence: The per-call timeout is a SIGALRM handler, which only runs between bytecodes. A C-level call that blocks (for example a catastrophic re backtrack or a huge integer power) cannot be cut off and uses up the batch budget. A call that ends the process (os._exit, a fatal signal, SIGXCPU at the CPU limit) leaves no output lines for later indices. Those indices keep the default ("timeout", None) although each call would have returned within 2 s on its own. For the reference this removes valid inputs and can push a task below 10 (not covered).
